subject: general
question: A train covers 400 km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 10 km/h more, it would have taken 2 h less for the same journey. Find the speed of the train.
solution:
**​Given:**

Distance covered = 400 km 

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance/Speed 

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the train be = a km/h 

As per the question; 

400/a - 400/(a + 10) = 2 

⇒ 1/a - 1/(a + 10) = 2/400 

⇒ (a + 10 - a)/a(a + 10) = 1/200

⇒ 10/a(a + 10) = 1/200

⇒ a² + 10a = 2000 

⇒ a2 + 10a - 2000 = 0

⇒ a2 + 50a - 40a - 2000 = 0

⇒ a(a + 50) - 40(a + 50) = 0

⇒ (a - 40)(a + 50) = 0

⇒ a = 40, a ≠ - 50

**∴ The speed of the train is 40 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**By Value Putting Method;

By using the following equation. 

⇒ 400/a - 400/(a + 10) = 2 

**Option 1: For a = 40, 400/40 - 400/(40 + 10) = 2 **

Option 2: For a = 50, 400/50 - 400/(50 + 10) ≠ 2

Option 3: For a = 55, 400/55 - 400/(55 + 10) ≠ 2

Option 4: For a = 45, 400/45 - 400/(45 + 10) ≠ 2
